ledger.reason: PMID38591662 measured binding of purified M. xanthus ImuA to short single-stranded DNA by fluorescence polarization and found nucleotide-dependent changes in affinity. PMID34190612 had not detected DNA binding using a different long-DNA mobility-shift assay. The later positive assay supports the claim under measured conditions; the earlier negative result is not evidence of universal absence. The accession bridge is documented by the primary promoter/genome sequence analysis.

Purified M. xanthus ImuA hydrolyzes ATP and its DNA-binding behavior responds to ADP and a nonhydrolyzable ATP analog in PMID38591662. These positive target-protein assays support ATP interaction independently of the generic RecA-domain mapping. ATP binding and ATP hydrolysis are distinct ontology claims, so binding is retained alongside the specific catalytic proposal.

Target-strain genetics and direct ImuB/RecA1 interactions in PMID34190612 support an accessory contribution to mutagenic lesion bypass, rather than establishing that ImuA itself catalyzes homologous recombination. Its physical regulatory activity supplies work in the process; it is not merely a necessary substrate. The imuA deletion reduced rather than abolished induced mutagenesis, so absolute indispensability is not asserted. GO0042276 specifies this mechanism. This is a branch correction: current GO does not place error-prone translesion synthesis under GO0006281, although the broad repair definition includes bypass.

PMID38591662 directly measured ATP turnover by purified M. xanthus ImuA using phosphate-release assays, with enhancement by single- and double-stranded DNA. This supports ATP hydrolysis activity. DNA stimulation alone does not establish ATP-dependent modification of DNA, helicase activity, or a demonstrated ATP-driven mutasome disassembly mechanism. The proposal is a molecular activity and is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of the existing ATP-binding claim.

limitation: Preservation accounting is not independent biological validation.
